coordinatorSummary: ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX, with 2 non-blocking advisories. Thirteen attacks run, two landed, both advisory-grade. Custody is intact: subject 5face6a9 at 0444 unmoved and valid JSON, predecessor v4 frozen at 09168659, HEAD never left d204ba0, file 08 and file 02 at their pins with a clean tree. This revision repairs my own v4 SHOULD-FIX using wording I suggested, which is the situation most likely to produce a lazy acceptance, so I tested it rather than recognised it: a programmatic scan of all fourteen classes for conditional language in owner and existingGate now returns zero, against exactly one at v4, and each of the four assertions in the replacement sentence was checked against live file 08 — DR-105's cell does name DR-G09 fixture execution as remaining, DR-G09's claim is the truthfulness of requested/granted/denied and enforced/disclosed outcomes, DR-G01..G05 measure something else, and DR-128 remains the home for demonstrated prevention. The repair took the stronger of the two branches I offered. My v4 advisory is also repaired: the v2FindingDisposition key is gone and a findingDisposition field carries the dispositions with landedAt pointers. I separately confirmed PPBSV3-B1 has not regressed — Codex's finding, which I wrongly cleared at v3 — by checking that EE-6b's invariant and pass, EE-5b, EE-7a and EE-7b are byte-identical to the v4 text I verified against permission-truth-tables.v9, D-032, the D-114 core-inventory contract and the live gate rows. The normalised diff confirms the revision is the smallest possible: two targeted edits plus version bookkeeping, with thirteen of fourteen classes and every other section untouched, and I re-verified the seven item names, the cell partition and the v1-slice quote against live sources rather than trusting that. The two advisories are that 'DR-G09 harness identifiers remain unauthored (D-086)' inverts what D-086 did — it recorded the identifiers; the harnesses are unauthored, as file 08's own DR-G09 cell shows — and that the renamed roster carries Claude's prior finding while both of Codex's prior findings occur nowhere in the artifact. Neither blocks, and I grade the first exactly as I graded v4's roster mislabel. My v3 advisory still stands and is unaffected: most classes are candidate-owned with no DR-G obligation, so DR-117 will not become D-056-eligible on this contract alone — planning information for the recording entry, not a defect here. This acceptance is of the artifact as an independently reviewed preview-scoped successor candidate only: it applies nothing, marks no row SATISFIED, opens no D-056 class, executes no class, and displaces neither v8 nor preview.v2.
